title: Listening lesson: Quebec news and TV
goal: By the end of this lesson you can follow the main points of a short Quebec news bulletin, recognise the key vocabulary of news, weather and traffic reports, and use Radio-Canada's OHdio and Le Téléjournal for daily listening practice.

body: *Radio-Canada* is the French-language public broadcaster. Its app *OHdio* has radio shows, podcasts (*balados*) and short news bulletins. *ICI Première* is its talk-and-news radio station.

*Le Téléjournal* is Radio-Canada's main evening TV news. Other sources: *TVA Nouvelles*, *RDI* (Radio-Canada's 24-hour news channel) and the free *Radio-Canada Info* app and website. Many shows have French subtitles (*sous-titres*), which help a lot.

News presenters use a careful, standard Quebec French: clear, close to international French, with Quebec vowels and the affricated *t* and *d* (*tu* → [tsu], *dire* → [dzire]). It is the best place to start before street French.

1. Before listening, read the headline and guess 5 words you expect. 2. Listen once for the general idea: who, what, where. 3. Listen again for numbers, dates and names. 4. Listen a third time with subtitles or a transcript. 5. Write down 3 new words and reuse them.
Short and daily beats long and rare: one 3-minute bulletin every day is worth more than one hour on Sunday.
Don't panic when you miss words. Focus on the words you know: numbers, place names, verbs in the passé composé (what happened) and the futur (what will happen).
learn.tip: Listen for the verbs: a passé composé tells you what happened, a futur tells you what's coming.

learn.h: The structure of a news bulletin
body: Bulletins follow the same order almost every time: greeting and headlines (*les manchettes*), the main stories, politics, international news, sports, then the weather (*la météo*) and sometimes traffic (*la circulation*).

Typical presenter phrases: *Bonsoir et bienvenue au Téléjournal*, *Voici les manchettes*, *On apprenait aujourd'hui que…* (We learned today that…), *Selon la police…* (According to the police…), *Passons maintenant à la météo*.

body: News uses the passé composé, the futur and the conditionnel. The conditionnel in the news means 'reportedly' (not confirmed): *Le suspect aurait quitté la ville* (The suspect reportedly left the city). For now, just recognise it.
Very frequent verbs: *annoncer* (to announce), *déclarer* (to declare), *se produire* (to happen), *blesser* (to injure), *augmenter* / *baisser* (to rise / to fall), *prévoir* (to forecast).

examples.en: Good evening and welcome to the Téléjournal.

examples.fr: Voici les manchettes de ce soir.
Le gouvernement du Québec a annoncé un nouveau plan pour le logement.
examples.en: The Quebec government announced a new housing plan.

examples.fr: Un accident s'est produit ce matin sur l'autoroute 40.
examples.en: An accident happened this morning on Highway 40.

examples.fr: Selon la police, deux personnes ont été blessées.
examples.en: According to the police, two people were injured.

examples.fr: Le prix de l'essence a augmenté de dix cents.
examples.en: The price of gas rose by ten cents.

examples.fr: Le Canadien a gagné quatre à deux contre Toronto.
examples.en: The Canadiens won four to two against Toronto.
examples.note: le Canadien = the Montreal hockey team

examples.fr: Environnement Canada prévoit vingt centimètres de neige.
examples.en: Environment Canada is forecasting twenty centimetres of snow.

examples.fr: Il y aura des averses en fin de journée.
examples.en: There will be showers late in the day.

examples.fr: Avec le facteur vent, on ressentira moins trente.
examples.en: With the wind chill, it will feel like minus thirty.

examples.fr: La circulation est dense sur le pont Jacques-Cartier.
examples.en: Traffic is heavy on the Jacques Cartier Bridge.
Let's move on to sports now.

examples.fr: Les citoyens sont invités à rester à la maison.
examples.en: Residents are asked to stay home.

examples.fr: J'écoute OHdio dans l'autobus tous les matins.
examples.en: I listen to OHdio on the bus every morning.

examples.fr: Je regarde le Téléjournal avec les sous-titres.
examples.en: I watch the Téléjournal with subtitles.

examples.fr: C'était tout pour ce bulletin. Bonne soirée!
examples.en: That's all for this bulletin. Good evening!

quebec.intro: Quebec news is your bridge between textbook French and street French. Presenters speak standard Quebec French; interviewees on the street often speak casually. Learn to hear both, and notice the Quebec words that even the news uses.

items.en: Traffic is heavy / It's jammed on the bridge.

items.qc: Le CH / le Tricolore / les Glorieux
items.note: Nicknames used in sports news and by fans
Speech: le monde = people, often with a plural verb (nonstandard)
Bordée is Quebec French, used even in weather reports
Quebec word, now standard; France often says un podcast

dialogue.fr: Bonsoir et bienvenue. Voici les manchettes de ce mardi.
dialogue.en: Good evening and welcome. Here are the headlines for this Tuesday.

dialogue.fr: Le gouvernement du Québec a annoncé aujourd'hui la construction de cinq mille logements à Montréal.
dialogue.en: The Quebec government announced today the construction of five thousand housing units in Montreal.

dialogue.fr: Un incendie s'est produit cette nuit dans un immeuble de Laval. Selon les pompiers, personne n'a été blessé.
dialogue.en: A fire broke out last night in a building in Laval. According to firefighters, no one was injured.

dialogue.fr: Sur les routes, la circulation est très dense sur le pont Champlain à cause d'un accident.
dialogue.en: On the roads, traffic is very heavy on the Champlain Bridge because of an accident.

dialogue.fr: En sports, le Canadien a battu Boston trois à un hier soir.
dialogue.en: In sports, the Canadiens beat Boston three to one last night.

dialogue.fr: Passons maintenant à la météo. Une bordée de neige est attendue demain.
dialogue.en: Now for the weather. A big snowfall is expected tomorrow.

dialogue.fr: Environnement Canada prévoit entre quinze et vingt-cinq centimètres de neige.
dialogue.en: Environment Canada is forecasting between fifteen and twenty-five centimetres of snow.

dialogue.fr: Avec le facteur vent, on ressentira moins vingt-huit.
dialogue.en: With the wind chill, it will feel like minus twenty-eight.

dialogue.fr: Soyez prudents sur les routes. C'était tout pour ce bulletin. Bonne soirée!
dialogue.en: Be careful on the roads. That's all for this bulletin. Good evening!

questions.q: Was anyone hurt in the Laval fire?

speak.prompt: Shadowing: play the bulletin line by line and repeat each sentence right after the speaker, copying the rhythm.
speak.model: Bonsoir et bienvenue. Voici les manchettes de ce mardi.

speak.prompt: Summarise the bulletin you heard in 3 sentences, in your own words.
speak.model: Le gouvernement va construire cinq mille logements à Montréal. Il y a eu un incendie à Laval, mais personne n'a été blessé. Demain, il va neiger beaucoup.

speak.prompt: Present tomorrow's weather like a newsreader.
speak.model: Demain, le ciel sera nuageux le matin. Il y aura des averses en après-midi. Maximum de douze degrés.

write.prompt: Listen to a real 3–5 minute Radio-Canada bulletin (OHdio or the Radio-Canada Info app). Write 5–6 sentences: the date, three stories you understood, the weather, and three new words.
write.model: J'ai écouté le bulletin de 7 h le 12 mars. D'abord, le gouvernement a annoncé un nouveau budget pour les écoles. Ensuite, il y a eu un accident sur l'autoroute 20. En sports, le Canadien a perdu contre Ottawa. Pour la météo, on prévoit de la pluie et cinq degrés. Nouveaux mots: une hausse, un député, la chaussée.

quiz.why: OHdio is Radio-Canada's app for radio and balados.

quiz.q: In the news, 'Le suspect aurait quitté la ville' means…
options: The suspect would leave the city.
The suspect reportedly left the city.
The suspect must leave the city.

quiz.q: Which order does a typical bulletin follow?
quiz.why: Headlines first, weather near the end.
Quebec word for a heavy snowfall.

quiz.q: The best listening habit at A2 is…
What does 'personne n'a été blessé' mean?
